canonical.question: Design an end-to-end analytics platform for a multi-tenant contact-center IVR system. You must ingest streaming JSON event logs from 40+ enterprise tenants with varying volumes (30,000–45,000 calls per day for mid-size tenants). The JSON contains multiple record types (call, transfer, prompt, intent, checkpoint, system, interaction) with nested arrays and unstable schemas that evolve over time. Requirements: (1) Dashboards covering a 16-month historical window with older data remaining retrievable but rarely queried; (2) Users need summary trends (hourly/daily) with drill-down capability to individual call records, and export functionality; (3) A subset of near-real-time dashboards must show data no more than 5 minutes old; (4) Strict tenant isolation with zero risk of cross-tenant data leaks; (5) Each tenant views dashboards in their own time zone. Design the architecture addressing: ingestion and schema drift handling, transformation engine choice and trade-offs, storage and serving layers for performance at scale, simultaneous batch and real-time pipelines, structural tenant isolation guarantees, hot vs. cold data strategy, multi-tenant deployment scaling, and infrastructure sizing and validation. Recommend AWS or Microsoft Fabric with justification.
canonical.title: Architecture — Multi-tenant IVR Analytics Platform
